settings.containerPortHint: The port the app listens on inside its container. Leave empty to detect it from the image automatically; set it (e.g. 5601 for OpenSearch Dashboards) only when the image exposes several ports or none. The IP:port link and every domain route target it. Applies on the next deploy.
settings.addADomainIntro: Pick how to expose this service - a free subdomain, your own domain with Let's Encrypt, or a Cloudflare/ngrok tunnel that needs no DNS or port-forwarding.
settings.subdomainTaken: That subdomain is already in use.
settings.tunnelUrl: That is a tunnel URL - it is already exposed by its tunnel, so it can't be added as a domain.
settings.rootDirectoryHint: Where this service lives in the repository. The build still gets the whole repository, so shared packages and the lockfile above it are available. Blank = the repository root.
settings.buildIntro: Polaris reads the repository and works these out - the framework, the package manager, and the workspace when there is one. Fill one in only to override what it found; the deployment log says what it detected.
settings.runtimeVersionHint: Node, Python, Go, Ruby, PHP or Java version to build on.
settings.outputDirectoryHint: For a built site, where its files end up.
settings.watchPathsHint: One glob per line. Deploy only when the push touched one of them, so a repository holding several services rebuilds just the ones that changed. Prefix with ! to exclude. Blank = any change.
settings.keepReleasesHint: Keep the last few versions running, each on its own address, while this service's own address stays on the newest. A service with a volume or on another server keeps the history but not the containers.
settings.containerPortShort: The port the app listens on inside its container. Blank detects it from the image.
settings.buildShort: Detected from the repository. Fill one in only to override it.
settings.autoDeployShort: Deploy each push to the branch, filtered by commit or path.
settings.watchPathsShort: One glob per line, ! to exclude. Blank means any change.
settings.keepReleasesShort: Earlier versions keep running, each on its own address.
settings.rootDirectoryShort: The folder this service lives in, for a repository holding several.
settings.waitForCiHint: Deploy a push only after all its GitHub checks pass. A commit with no checks deploys after a minute.
settings.ciGapApp: The GitHub App does not ask for the Checks permission, so nothing would ever deploy. On GitHub, open the App's Permissions & events, set Checks to Read-only and save.
settings.ciGapInstall: The GitHub App's installation on this repository has not accepted the Checks permission yet. Open it on GitHub and accept the new permissions.
settings.ciGapEvents: The GitHub App does not send check suite events, so checks are read once a minute instead. To hear about them at once, tick Check suite under Subscribe to events in the App's settings.
settings.ciGapAdmins: GitHub does not let Polaris read this repository's checks yet, so nothing would deploy. Your administrators can allow it.

exposureHint.zoneBase: A hostname straight on {host}, with a Let's Encrypt certificate. This one is not covered by a wildcard, so it needs its own DNS record - Polaris writes it when the domain sits in your connected Cloudflare account, and otherwise tells you the record to add. For a name on a different domain, pick Custom domain.
exposureHint.zone: A hostname on your own domain, covered by the zone's wildcard record - no DNS to add, with a Let's Encrypt certificate. Choose the subdomain, or take a random one for an unguessable URL. Each build also gets this name with its commit added. For a name on a domain that is not listed, pick Custom domain.
exposureHint.subdomain: Always reachable: a free sslip.io subdomain that resolves on any device (a public Let's Encrypt name on a reachable box). Behind NAT, Polaris also starts a free Cloudflare quick link so it works from outside. Connect a Cloudflare account or a custom domain for a stable public URL.
exposureHint.local: A friendly {example} address, LOCAL only - it resolves on your LAN via mDNS (works on macOS/iOS and most modern devices; Windows may not resolve it, use the free subdomain there). Trusted HTTPS once you install the CA root (Admin - Domains).
exposureHint.custom: Any hostname on any domain - {hostname} on your own, or a different domain entirely. Polaris writes the DNS record itself when the domain sits in your connected Cloudflare account; otherwise point it at this server. The certificate is issued automatically either way.
exposureHint.duckdnsMissing: Configure DuckDNS under Integrations first, then pick a subdomain here.
exposureHint.duckdns: Just the subdomain - the base is your DuckDNS domain. It resolves via DuckDNS with a Let's Encrypt certificate automatically.
exposureHint.proxy: For a domain fronted by an external proxy that terminates TLS.
exposureHint.cfNamedConnected: Polaris creates the tunnel and the DNS record for you - just enter a hostname on a domain in your Cloudflare account.
exposureHint.cfNamed: Create the tunnel in Cloudflare and paste its connector token. Tip: connect a Cloudflare API token under Integrations to skip this - then you only pick a hostname.
exposureHint.cfQuick: A throwaway *.trycloudflare.com URL - no account, no DNS, no port-forwarding. The link changes each time it starts.
exposureHint.ngrok: A public ngrok URL forwarded to this app. Add your ngrok authtoken under Integrations first; ngrok's free plan allows one tunnel at a time.
exposureHint.tcp: Publishes a port of the container on a public port of the server, as raw TCP: a database, a game, a broker. HTTP domains keep working beside it.

servedBy.label: Who answers these addresses
servedBy.polarisHint: Point the DNS at Polaris. It forwards each request to {server}, so while Polaris is down or unreachable these addresses stop answering. Worth it for a server that cannot hold a public address of its own.
servedBy.serverHint: Point the DNS at {server}. It serves these addresses itself, so they keep working while Polaris is switched off, updating, or unreachable.

moveOut.heading: Move it to Vercel or Railway
moveOut.body: They build and serve it from the same repository; the variables go with it, and it stays on this project's board. Nothing here is deleted - it is stopped, and one button starts it again.

danger.queued: Already queued. Deploy the pending changes to carry it out, or discard it from the banner.
danger.hint: Removes the container, its domains, variables and deploy history.
danger.description: The container, its domains, variables and deploy history go. Nothing happens until you deploy the pending changes.

server.label: Where this service runs
server.hint: Move the service to another connected server. Connect more under Servers. Changing this stops the current container on the old server; redeploy to bring it up on the new one.

scaling.unreadable: Could not read how this service is scaled
scaling.savedRedeploying: Saved. The service is being started again with the new settings.
scaling.title: Scaling
scaling.copiesHint: How many copies of the service run at once, up to {max}. The edge spreads requests over them.
scaling.autoscaleHint: Add a copy when CPU or requests per copy stay above their target for three minutes, and take one away after ten minutes with both low. With a requests target, {minutes} minutes with no requests at all drops straight to the fewest. CPU is each copy's share of the machine, the same figure the Metrics tab shows.
scaling.notOnSwarm: Not on a swarm machine, which keeps its own count.
scaling.sleepHint: Stop the service after a stretch with no visits, and start it on the next one. The first visitor sees a page saying it is waking up for the few seconds that takes.
scaling.resourcesHint: A copy past its memory is stopped and started again; one past its CPU is slowed. Blank = no limit.
scaling.sticky: Keep each visitor on one copy
scaling.stickyHint: For WebSockets and sessions kept in memory. A cookie pins the visitor to the copy that answered them first.
scaling.healthPathHint: Asked of every copy every 10 seconds. One that stops answering is left out until it answers again. Blank = no check.
scaling.emailShield: With more than one copy the edge balances between them itself, so email addresses in its pages are not hidden from scrapers.
scaling.balancingShort: How the edge spreads visitors over the copies.
scaling.autoscaleShort: Adds and removes copies to follow CPU or traffic.
scaling.sleepShort: Stops it when nobody visits and wakes it on the next visit.

private.named: Also allow these people, groups and roles
private.needsAudience: Choose who may open this address.

behaviour.title: Deploys
behaviour.loadFailed: Could not read how this service deploys

mode.overlap: The new version starts beside the running one. The edge moves to it once it answers on its port, then the old one is drained and stopped. If it does not come up, the old one keeps serving.
mode.kept: Each version runs on its own, and the edge moves to the newest once it answers on its port.
mode.swarm: Swarm starts the new task before stopping the old one and rolls back by itself if it fails.

reason.hostPort: It binds port {port}/{protocol} on the server, and two versions cannot hold one port. Turn off the open port under Networking if only the domain needs to reach it.
reason.volumes: It keeps data on {names}. Two copies of a program that locks or writes one file there can fail or corrupt it, so the old one is stopped first.
reason.newVolumes: This deploy creates {names}, so it restarts this once. Deploys after it have no gap.
reason.compose: It runs your own compose file, whose names Polaris does not change.
reason.edge: This server's edge does not take routes from Polaris yet. Prepare it on the server's page.
reason.history: It keeps its previous versions, which only run side by side on the Polaris host.
reason.unreadable: Its settings could not be read. Save them again.

behaviour.overlapHint: For uploads or a cache. Leave off for a database or anything that locks its data folder: two copies would hold the same files for a few seconds.
behaviour.networksHint: Docker networks already on the server that this service joins on its next deploy, with the names other containers there call it by ({name} when left empty). Polaris never creates or removes them.

publicNet.title: Public Networking
publicNet.intro: Access your application over HTTP with the following domains, or over raw TCP.
publicNet.targetPort: Enter the port your app is listening on
publicNet.portScanning: Looking for the ports it listens on...
publicNet.portSeen: These are the ports it was seen listening on just now.
publicNet.portConfigured: It is not running, or its image cannot be asked, so this is the port it is set to.
publicNet.dialsPort: Traffic to this address goes to port {port} of the service.
publicNet.serviceStopped: The service is stopped, so this address shows a not-running page.
publicNet.dnsProxied: Cloudflare proxy detected. The address it resolves to is Cloudflare's, so where it ends up cannot be read from here.
publicNet.dnsMissing: Waiting for DNS. Create one of these records at your DNS provider.
publicNet.dnsElsewhere: DNS points somewhere else ({addresses}). Change the record to one of these.
publicNet.recordPreferred: Recommended: follows the service if the server's address changes.
publicNet.recordOr: Or point it straight at the server.
publicNet.propagationHint: A new record can take from minutes to a few hours to be seen everywhere. This check runs again each time the panel opens.
publicNet.apexHint: This is the top of its domain, where DNS allows no CNAME. An A record works with every provider; an ALIAS or a flattened CNAME also works where your provider offers one.
publicNet.wildcardHint: A wildcard covers every name under it. Its certificate is issued over DNS through a connected Cloudflare account (the _acme-challenge record is written for you); on any other DNS provider, upload a certificate for it with the shield button.
publicNet.cloudflareHint: Keep Cloudflare's SSL/TLS mode on Full or Full (strict). Flexible sends plain HTTP here, which this server redirects to HTTPS, and the visitor loops forever.
publicNet.certPending: Certificate not issued yet. Let's Encrypt issues it once DNS points here.
publicNet.certFailed: The certificate could not be issued. It is retried on its own.
publicNet.certUntrusted: Serving a certificate browsers do not trust yet, while the real one is issued.
publicNet.certValid: Certificate valid for {days} more days. Renewed automatically 30 days before it expires.
publicNet.certValidIssuer: Certificate from {issuer}, valid for {days} more days. Renewed automatically 30 days before it expires.
publicNet.alsoTunnelHint: A tunnel serves this name too. Remove this entry to keep only the tunnel.
publicNet.tcpForward: Behind a router: forward TCP {ports} to {lan} for these to answer from outside your network.
publicNet.tcpApply: The change takes effect when the service is next started.
publicNet.certUnknown: The certificate could not be read from here. It shows once the address answers this server.

checks.title: Pre-flight
checks.noAddress: There is no public address to point the record at.
checks.sameEdge: Both services answer at the same address, so only the route moves.
checks.noAnswer: Nothing answered when asked from here. Some routers do not loop their own address back, so this does not stop the move.
checks.notRouted: Its server has no route for {hostname} yet.
checks.answersBadly: It answers for {hostname} with an error (HTTP {code}).
checks.tlsReady: A certificate already covers the name there.
checks.tlsOnSwitch: The certificate is issued once the record points there, so HTTPS may warn for a minute after the switch.

failure.sameService: That is the service serving it already. Choose another one.
failure.notDeployed: {target} has never been deployed. Deploy it, then try again.
failure.notRunning: {target} is not running. Start or redeploy it, then try again.
failure.notRouted: The server {target} runs on did not pick up the route for {hostname}. Wait a minute and try again; if it repeats, redeploy {target}.
failure.down: {target} answered {hostname} with an error (HTTP {code}). Fix it, then try again.
failure.noAddress: The server {target} runs on has no public address. Give it one in its server settings, then try again.
failure.recordWrite: Cloudflare refused the record change. Check that the DNS connection can still edit this zone, then switch again.
failure.routeMove: The route could not be moved to {target}. Switch again; if it repeats, redeploy {target}.
failure.rollbackWrite: Cloudflare refused to put the record back, so the move is still open. Check that the DNS connection can still edit this zone, then roll back again.
failure.rollbackRoute: The route could not be moved back, so the move is still open. Roll back again in a minute.
failure.timeout: After 48 hours the public resolvers still do not all see the new address. Roll back, or check the record at your DNS provider.

cutover.checking: Checking {target} before anything changes. If this does not move on, roll back and start again.
cutover.lowering: The TTL went from {old} to {ttl} seconds. Caches let go of the old answer by {time}. Switching now works too; it only settles more slowly.
cutover.manualIntro: This domain's DNS is not managed here. At your DNS provider:
cutover.manualLower: Lower the record's TTL to {ttl} seconds and wait {old} seconds, so caches let go of the old answer.
cutover.manualTtlShort: The TTL is already short, so there is nothing to wait for.
cutover.manualChange: Change the record to this, with a TTL of {ttl} seconds, then press the button below:
cutover.readyEdge: Both services answer at the same address, so DNS stays as it is and only the route moves.
cutover.readyCloudflare: Polaris changes the record to {address} for you when you switch.
cutover.propagating: Waiting for the change to reach everyone. {source} keeps answering whoever still has the old address.
cutover.progress: {agree} of {total} public resolvers see the new address
cutover.targetWaiting: {target} does not answer for the name yet.
cutover.finishing: Everything agrees. Handing the domain over...
cutover.doneTtl: The TTL is back to {ttl} seconds.
cutover.doneManualTtl: You can put the TTL back to {ttl} seconds at your DNS provider.
cutover.rollbackBody: {hostname} goes back to {source}, the way it was before.
cutover.rollbackBodyManual: {hostname} goes back to {source}. Change the record back at your DNS provider too; the old values are shown next.
cutover.rolledBackManual: Change the record back at your DNS provider:

gpu.swarm: A service on a swarm cluster cannot be given a card.
gpu.notUsing: Not holding any GPU memory right now.

deployHooks.title: Deploy hooks
deployHooks.description: Signed URLs that redeploy this service when your CI or registry posts to them.
deployHooks.guard: The URL alone is not enough: every request must be signed with the secret, sent within five minutes, and is accepted once.
deployHooks.empty: No deploy hooks for this service yet.
deployHooks.loadFailed: Deploy hooks could not be loaded.
deployHooks.name: Name
deployHooks.rotateQuestion: Requests to {name} must be signed with the new secret from now on. The URL stays the same.
deployHooks.removeQuestion: Remove {name}? Anything still posting to its URL is refused from now on.
deployHooks.dialogDescription: Polaris redeploys this service each time a correctly signed request arrives, for as long as you may deploy it.
deployHooks.secretDescription: Copy it now. It is shown only this once; if you lose it, make a new one.
deployHooks.secretVerify: Sign each POST the same way: X-Polaris-Timestamp (unix seconds, within 5 minutes), a unique X-Polaris-Delivery id, and X-Polaris-Signature: sha256= followed by the hex HMAC-SHA256 of the timestamp, a dot and the raw body.
deployHooks.othersHint: They count toward your maximum of {max}.

errors.rateLimited: Too many tries. Wait a few minutes and try again.
errors.limit: You have the maximum of {max} deploy hooks.
errors.notFound: That deploy hook no longer exists.

security.found: {count, plural, one {# critical vulnerability} other {# critical vulnerabilities}} with a known fix:
security.refused: This service blocks such releases, so this one did not go live.
security.confirmBody: The same commit goes live with the vulnerabilities its image scan found. Your name and the time are recorded on the new deployment.
security.blockShort: Hold back a release whose image has a critical vulnerability with a known fix.
security.blockHint: Checked against the latest scan of the same image on this server. Off, such a release still goes live and carries a warning. A held-back release can be deployed anyway from its row, and who did it is recorded.
